title: Physical or sexual abuse is a crime handled by the police
sourceTitle: MOM – Abuse and ill-treatment of a foreign domestic worker
text:
MOM takes abuse very seriously, **especially physical or sexual abuse**. Abuse cases are **investigated by the police**.

Employers convicted of abusing a domestic worker face severe penalties, and they and their spouses are **permanently banned** from employing another domestic worker.
quote: If you suspect that an FDW is being abused or ill-treated, report the matter to the police. Complaints of abuse are investigated by the police.

title: Your sleeping place must be safe and decent
sourceTitle: MOM – Rest days, health and well-being for migrant domestic workers
text: Where you sleep must **protect you from sun, rain and strong winds**. You must be given at least **a mattress, a pillow and a blanket**, as well as bathroom amenities and toiletries.
quote: The accommodation must adequately protect your MDW from environmental elements such as sun, rain or strong winds.

title: You must be given 3 meals a day
sourceTitle: MOM – Rest days, health and well-being for migrant domestic workers
text:
Your employer must give you **3 meals a day**, with enough food for the work you do (for example rice or bread, vegetables, and meat or fish).

Your employer should respect food you cannot eat because of your **religion or dietary needs**. Not being given enough food is a problem you can report to MOM (see "How to report a problem to MOM").
quote: You must provide your MDW with 3 meals a day.

title: If you are in danger or in distress
sourceTitle: MOM – I am a migrant domestic worker (MDW) in distress. Who can I call?
text:
If you are **in danger, call the Police at 999**.

If you are in distress but not in immediate danger, you can call MOM's **Migrant Domestic Worker Helpline at 1800 339 5505** (Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm) to speak to an MOM officer. Mobile airtime charges may apply.
quote: Call the Police at 999 if you are in danger.

title: How to report a problem to MOM
sourceTitle: MOM – What should I do if an MDW has not been paid, is overworked or not given enough food?
text:
There are several ways to report a problem like unpaid salary, overwork or not enough food:
1. **Report online** through MOM's website.
2. **Call the MOM Migrant Domestic Worker Helpline**: 1800 339 5505 (Mon–Fri, 8.30am–5.30pm).
3. **Call the Centre for Domestic Employees (CDE)**: 1800 2255 233, open 24 hours.
4. **Go in person** to the MOM Services Centre, Hall A, 1500 Bendemeer Road, Singapore 339946.
quote: You can report the infringement online.

title: Ill-treatment includes mental and emotional abuse
sourceTitle: MOM – Does ill-treatment of a foreign employee include mental or emotional abuse?
text:
Abuse is not only hitting. MOM says ill-treatment includes **physical and sexual abuse, and also mental and emotional abuse**, and an employer neglecting your well-being.

All employers must treat their workers with care and respect. If convicted of ill-treatment, employers may be fined, jailed or both, and may be banned from hiring workers.
quote: Other than physical and sexual abuse, this also include mental and emotional abuse.

title: Your employer must pay for your medical care
sourceTitle: MOM – Can I get my MDW to co-pay her medical expenses that exceed the insurance benefit limit?
text: Your employer must bear **all medical costs necessary for your health**. **You cannot be made to pay for your own medical expenses**, even the part above what the insurance pays.
quote: You are not allowed to make your MDW pay for her medical expenses. This includes medical expenses that are part of, or above what the insurance pays.

title: Your passport belongs to you
sourceTitle: MOM – Can an employer keep a worker's passport?
text:
Your employer **should not keep your passport** and should not force you to give it to them. Your passport belongs to you (and your country's government), not to your employer.

A good employer gives you a safe place to keep it, such as a locker, and you must be able to reach it at any time. If your employer insists on holding your passport, you can contact MOM for help.
quote: Employers should not keep the passports of their migrant workers or migrant domestic workers (MDWs). They should also not force their workers to give them their passport.

title: Your phone is your personal property
sourceTitle: MOM – Ask Jaya: I want to give my MDW access to her phone
text:
MOM says your mobile phone is **your personal property** and you should have access to it. It is how you stay in touch with your family.

Your employer may agree **house rules with you** about *when* you use your phone, for example not while cooking, looking after children or giving medicine. Having rules about timing is normal. Being cut off from your phone completely is not what MOM describes.
quote: A mobile phone is the personal property of your migrant domestic worker (MDW) and she should have access to it.

title: Your right to privacy when you sleep and change
sourceTitle: MOM – Rest days, health and well-being for migrant domestic workers
text:
You **must not be made to sleep in the same room as a male adult or teenager**. MOM says employers should give you a separate room if possible.

Cameras **must not be placed where they compromise your privacy or modesty**, for example where you sleep, change clothes, or in the bathroom.
quote: Your MDW must not sleep in the same room as a male adult or teenager.

title: If you work on your rest day, you must be paid extra
sourceTitle: MOM – Rest days, health and well-being for migrant domestic workers
text:
If you agree to work on one of your rest days, your employer must pay you **at least one extra day's salary** for that day.

This money is **in addition to** your normal monthly salary. It is not part of your basic salary.
quote: You must compensate her with at least 1 day's salary.

title: At least one rest day a month cannot be replaced with money
sourceTitle: MOM – Rest days, health and well-being for migrant domestic workers
text:
Every month, you must get **at least one rest day that cannot be "bought back"** with extra pay. Even if you agree to work on your other rest days, this one rest day a month must be a real day off.

If you could not take your rest day in a month, it can be moved to the next month (deferred by up to one month). Employers who do not give the mandatory rest day may face enforcement action from MOM.
quote: You must ensure that your MDW has at least one rest day per month that cannot be compensated away.

title: You are entitled to one rest day every week
sourceTitle: MOM – Rest days, health and well-being for migrant domestic workers
text:
You have the right to **one rest day every week**. You and your employer should agree together which day of the week it is.

Your rest day can be taken as one full day, or as two half days. It is your rest day, so you can choose to go out or to spend it at home.
quote: The rest day can be taken as one full day or over two half days.

title: Your salary cannot be lower than what was declared to MOM
sourceTitle: MOM – Paying the salary of a foreign domestic worker
text:
The salary you receive **must not be lower than the amount your employer declared to MOM** when applying for your Work Permit.

If you are being paid less than what was agreed and declared, you can ask MOM for help (see "How to report a problem to MOM").
quote: The salary must not be lower than what you declared to MOM.

title: Your employer must not keep your salary, money or bank card
sourceTitle: MOM – Paying the salary of a foreign domestic worker
text:
Your employer **must not keep your salary or any other money that belongs to you**, even if you ask them to keep it for you. They also must not keep your bank book or bank card.

This rule has applied since 1 January 2019. It protects you from losing access to your own money.
quote: You must not keep your FDW's salary or any other money belonging to her, even if she requests for it.

title: Your salary must be paid every month, within 7 days
sourceTitle: MOM – Paying the salary of a foreign domestic worker
text:
Your employer must pay your salary **every month**. It must be paid **no later than 7 days after the end of the salary period**. For example, salary for 1–31 May must be paid by 7 June.

A salary period cannot be longer than one month, so salary should not be held back and paid months later.
quote: You must pay your FDW her salary every month, no later than 7 days after the last day of the salary period.

title: Salary records and paying into your own bank account
sourceTitle: MOM – Paying the salary of a foreign domestic worker
text:
You can ask for your salary to be paid **directly into your own bank account**, and your employer must do this if you request it. The account must be yours. It cannot be a joint account with your employer.

If you are paid in cash, there must be a **salary record that both you and your employer sign** each time. Keeping your own copy or photo of these records can help if there is a problem later.
quote: You must pay your FDW via direct bank transfer if she requests for it.

title: What you can do if your salary has not been paid
sourceTitle: MOM – How can an MDW report that her salary has not been paid?
text:
If your salary has not been paid, you can contact MOM's **Migrant Domestic Worker Helpline at 1800 339 5505** (+65 6339 5505 from overseas), Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm.

MOM can help you **recover your salary through conciliation**, a process where MOM helps you and your employer reach a solution. Your salary records and any messages about payment can help.
quote: 1800 339 5505 or +65 6339 5505 for overseas callers. (Operating hours: Mon – Fri, 8.30am to 5.30pm)

title: Organisations that support domestic workers
sourceTitle: CDE – Contact us; HOME – Homepage
text:
You do not have to handle this alone. Two organisations that help domestic workers:
- **Centre for Domestic Employees (CDE)**: a 24-hour toll-free helpline, 1800 2255 233, for help with employment problems.
- **HOME (Humanitarian Organisation for Migration Economics)**: a charity with a Domestic Worker Helpline at +65 9787 3122 (call or WhatsApp). See home.org.sg.
quote: 24-hour Helpline (Toll-free): 1800 2255 233 (1800-CALL-CDE)

title: Changing to a new employer
sourceTitle: MOM – Transfer a migrant domestic worker (MDW) directly to a new employer
text:
To move directly to a new employer, the **new employer applies to MOM** and asks your **current employer to give consent** through MOM's online service. Both steps must be done at least 30 days before your Work Permit expires. When the new Work Permit is issued, the old one is cancelled.

This process depends on your current employer agreeing. If you are being mistreated and want to leave, talk to MOM, CDE or HOME about your options first.

title: You should only do housework for your own employer
sourceTitle: MOM – Employment rules for migrant domestic workers
text:
Under your Work Permit, you can **only do domestic (household) work**, and **only for your employer at the home address declared to MOM**. Your employer should not send you to work in their business or shop, or to clean other people's homes.

Your employer can be penalised for this, with a financial penalty of up to $10,000. (Looking after a child at a relative's home is only allowed in special cases that the employer must tell MOM about first.)
quote: Can only work for her employer at the residential address declared to MOM.
